business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Commodity Trade in Whole and Skimmed Milk Powder

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16 (OBCA), ss. 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 107, 114.1; alternative: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 4, 6, 101, 106 (if federal incorporation is preferred)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (Ontario Business Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under OBCA; directors must fix the consideration for issued shares at not less than nominal value; no escrow account is mandated for an ordinary dairy trading corporation, and funds may be held in a standard commercial banking account; a NUANS name search is required if a distinctive name is used
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the corporation accept the proffered share subscriptions and allot the initial common shares to the named subscribers at par value; that the registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, within Ontario; that the draft by-laws be adopted; that [Name], [Name], and [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, respectively, with authority to execute banking and regulatory filings; that banking resolutions and leasing agreements be approved; and that all actions already taken to incorporate the corporation be ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NUANS Search Provider coordinated through the Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed NUANS search house to conduct a name search in respect of the proposed corporate name. Verify distinctiveness and compliance with OBCA name rules, and request a reservation or submit the NUANS report with the subsequent incorporation filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or confusingly similar, file a fresh NUANS report for an alternate name, or proceed with a numbered corporation and subsequently apply for a name change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) through the online Ontario Business Registry portal. Specify the authorized share structure, including unlimited common and restricted voting classes, list the initial directors, provide the Ontario registered office address, attach the NUANS report, and pay the statutory filing fee of CAD 360.
required_dossiers: Registered office address consent if not immediate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, rectify the stated defect (e.g., revised share conditions, corrected director consents, or amended name) and resubmit. If the name is refused, convert the filing to a numbered corporation and file a later Articles of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Establishment of Corporate Record Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the official Certificate of Incorporation and Articles. Immediately prepare the corporate minute book, including by-laws, share certificates, register of directors, register of shareholders, and minutes of organizational meetings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If errors appear in the certificate (e.g., legal name, date, or address), file a Request for Correction with the registry within 30 days; otherwise, maintain the erroneous document as incorporated and proceed by Articles of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a Business Number (BN) and open accounts for corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll source deductions (if employees), and an import/export account (RMDOT) sufficient for cross-border raw milk powder trade. Complete RC1 and RC85 forms electronically.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the application, contact the Business Inquiries line, supply corrected ownership or address details, and resubmit the account registration forms; expedited processing is available for dairy commodity importers by phone.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Ontario Initial Return and Ongoing Registry Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days of incorporation, file the Ontario Initial Return pursuant to OBCA s. 114.1, confirming the registered office address, the directors' names and addresses, and the officer information. File subsequent annual returns on time.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Initial Return is filed late or marked deficient, promptly submit a corrected return and, if an administrative notice is issued, request leniency or abatement of any late-filing penalty via a written explanation to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or sign unanimous written consents) to approve the pro-forma First Board Resolution, adopt by-laws, accept share subscription agreements, appoint officers, ratify the bank account mandate, and authorize opening of trading accounts for dairy commodity transactions.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting or written consent
Banking resolution and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any procedural defect is identified, ratify the action by a subsequent unanimous director resolution and record the curative minutes in the corporate minute book.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) and Ontario Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (OMAFRA) – Dairy Commodity Trade Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFC) License for Import/Export of Dairy Products (Food Business License – Class: Dairy) and, where supply-managed product is involved, an Import Permit under the Export and Import Permits Act issued by Global Affairs Canada

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Screening (Category C – Low Impact): wholesale dairy storage and distribution facilities are generally exempt from a full Environmental Assessment if no significant site alteration occurs; an Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA) is required only if stationary equipment (e.g., ammonia refrigeration, boilers, or emergency generators) causes contaminant discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Air emissions, including ammonia from cold storage systems, must comply with O. Reg. 419/05 point-of-impingement concentration limits and the Toxic Substances Management Policy; wastewater discharges to municipal sewer must conform to the local Sewer Use By-law and Ontario Water Resources Act, with typical pH range 6.0-9.0 and total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L; any VOC emissions from cleaning agents must be reported if above 250 tonnes per year under the EPA National Pollutant Release Inventory threshold; waste dairy powder must be managed as non-hazardous solid waste under O. Reg. 347

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07), including smoke detection and extinguisher placement; structural load inspection and building permit clearance under the Ontario Building Code Act, 1992; occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA) for warehouse racking, forklift operations, and cold storage protocols; WSIB workplace registration; and a Ministry of Labour inspection clearance for any mechanical refrigeration plant of greater than 500 kW.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account; Ontario Ministry of Finance (for provincial tax policy, with GST/HST administered by the CRA)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident / foreign entity engaged in taxable activity in Canada must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA, which serves as the GST/HST registration ID. Registration can be completed online through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO), by submitting Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number', or by mailing/faxing the equivalent paper application. Supporting documentation includes proof of foreign incorporation, foreign tax identification number, director/officer details, principal Canadian business premises, and estimated Canadian taxable revenue. The BN is used for all federal program accounts (income tax, GST/HST, payroll, import/export). A foreign entity whose supplies are exclusively zero-rated may elect to register voluntarily to claim input tax credits on related expenses.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a U.S.-style check-the-box entity classification regime; a Business Corporation is automatically a separate taxable entity at the corporate level. Statutory elections relevant to cross-border trading structures include: (i) the Excise Tax Act s.156 election to treat certain supplies among closely related corporations as made for nil consideration for GST/HST purposes; (ii) the Income Tax Act s.216 election for a non-resident to file and pay Canadian income tax on a net basis for rental / timber income; (iii) the s.93(2) election to deem dividends from a foreign affiliate to be received out of taxable surplus; and (iv) association elections under s.256 of the Income Tax Act affecting allocation of small business deduction limits. Hybrid mismatch rules apply mandatorily and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CA$30,000 (the small supplier threshold — the value of worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada during the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; once exceeded over a calendar quarter, mandatory registration is required).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping regime is currently in force for GST/HST. Taxpayers may issue electronic invoices provided they are legible, complete, and stored in a CRA-compliant format. Ontario does not maintain a separate clearance system. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing standard (Peppol) is voluntary.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods that meet the definition of a 'qualified export' under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act (e.g., ETA s.1, s.2, s.3), including goods exported directly by the supplier or delivered to a common carrier for export, and to certain intangible personal property supplied to non-residents for use solely outside Canada. Services are zero-rated under Schedule VII where they are supplied to a non-resident and are not for consumption in Canada (subject to exceptions for services in connection with Canadian real property or goods). The supplier must retain contemporaneous documentary evidence proving export or offshore supply within the required evidentiary window; otherwise the supply is recharacterized as taxable at the HST rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or electronic filing through the Canadian Export Reporting System / CERS)
Bill of Lading (straight or order) or Air Waybill
Commercial Invoice and detailed Packing List
Evidence of export issued by the carrier or customs office (e.g., cargo control document, terminal receipt, customs stamp)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank wire transfer confirmation showing foreign currency payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the CRA determines that an export zero-rating claim was unsupported, the supply is reclassified as taxable and the taxpayer is liable for the unremitted HST (currently 13% in Ontario) plus interest under Excise Tax Act s.280. Civil penalties include failure-to-register and false-statement penalties under ETA s.285 and gross negligence penalties under s.285.1, which can be up to 50% of the tax sought. CRA may claw back GST/HST input tax credits claimed on inputs relating to the failed export, for a period of up to four years (or longer in the case of misrepresentation or fraud). Fraudulent export zero-rating may also lead to criminal prosecution under ETA s.397, with fines up to 200% of the amount evaded and imprisonment. Although Canadian law does not prescribe a statutory repatriation deadline for export proceeds, the 180-day benchmark is commonly used as a documentary evidence-preservation period for corroborating payment and export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary authority; foreign-exchange administration is functionally shared with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for bank prudential conduct and with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for cross-border payment monitoring under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), together with the Department of Finance Canada for exchange-rate policy under the Currency Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange-rate regime; Canada complies with IMF Article VIII and imposes no exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, royalties, and capital repatriation by non-resident shareholders are freely permitted, subject solely to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25% statutory, reduced to 5% on dividends under the Canada–[Resident Country] tax treaty with form NR301/NR302 filing) and to FINTRAC reporting for each wire transfer equal to or above CAD 10,000. No prior regulatory approval is required for the conversion of CAD into foreign currency or for the crediting of foreign currency to domestic or offshore accounts, provided the bank-facing documentation supports the underlying trade or investment purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation to surrender, repatriate, or convert export receipts in Canada; exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely in domestic, cross-border, or offshore accounts. The only compliance obligations are: (i) a Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) B13A export declaration for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000, submitted within 15 days after the export event; (ii) an International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) / Statistics Canada classification of the inward remittance as 'trade settlement' or 'direct investment' as requested by the receiving bank; and (iii) FINTRAC reporting of any single cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more, in addition to ongoing record‑keeping and beneficial-ownership transparency obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational CAD/USD multicurrency account and segregated Capital Escrow sub-account for import/export settlements
Operational Business Account with cross-border treasury module and USD clearing facility
Operational Account plus Trade Finance desk for commercial letters of credit and documentary collections
Operational Account and Escrow Account for capital subscriptions and third-party disbursement verification
Operational Account with SWIFT-based wire origination and integrated FX hedging line
Operational Account with limited provincial network; suitable for secondary treasury support

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary payment streams and Low for principal trade settlements. Non-bank fintechs and digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) may operate as money services businesses (MSBs) in Canada under FINTRAC registration, but they cannot issue commercial letters of credit, are not members of the Lynx/ACSS clearing system, and hold funds in non-bank pooled/omnibus accounts that do not meet escrow-grade segregation expectations of Canadian and foreign dairy counterparties. They are legally constrained by the Bank Act (prohibition on engaging in the business of banking without a Schedule I/II charter) and by PCMLTFA requirements for MSB registration; therefore, their use should be limited to low-value disbursements to service providers, not to LC-based commodity purchase contracts from ISO/IEC-accredited dairy processors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Ontario business corporation with non-resident beneficial owners and high-velocity cross-border commodity flows, the six tier‑1 Schedule I banks generally mandate an in‑person onboarding interview for at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner (or a delegated officer under a board resolution); remote identification is permissible under FINTRAC's two‑step identity verification only where the client has a pre-existing relationship or where an accredited notary/lawyer attests to identity, but Canadian banks' enterprise risk policies typically require physical presence for accounts receiving export proceeds above CAD 250,000 annually. Directors should therefore plan for an in-branch KYC interview at the chosen bank's Toronto or international financial centre branch, with original passports, corporate resolution, and certified corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure involving foreign nominees or a trust holding the Ontario corporation's shares
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Business Information Report (corporate registry extract from the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery), trust deed and trustee declarations, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) attestation form, organizational chart tracing at least 25% beneficial ownership, source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, audited financial statements of the subscriber), and a Canadian legal opinion confirming no bearer shares or unregistered holdings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wires to/from jurisdictions perceived as higher-risk for dairy commodity trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sales and purchase agreements for whole and skimmed milk powder, commercial invoices and packing lists, bills of lading and air waybills, certificates of origin and phytosanitary certificates, product specification sheets, CFIA export certification, marine/transit insurance policies, and a correspondent bank reference letter from the foreign buyer's/seller's financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence or inconsistency of statutory licenses for dairy commodity export
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA) Licence from the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), Canadian Dairy Commission registration or export permit for butter/skim milk powder quotas, import-country health certificates and pre-export inspection reports, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) certification, and the company's dairy dealer agreement with a licensed processor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for third-party payments where the remitter is not the named commercial counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Back-to-back supply chain agreements, subrogation or assignment notices, invoice genealogy demonstrating the third-party payment mirrors an outstanding receivable/payable, board-approved treasury policy permitting directed payments, reconciliation ledger between invoice numbers, payment amounts, and SWIFT reference numbers, and a signed indemnity from the third-party remitter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hit or politically exposed person (PEP) status of a shareholder, director, or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-media search results from a reputable due-diligence provider, verification against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions sanctions lists, Global Affairs Canada and United Nations sanctions registries, PEP self-declaration and source-of-wealth/income documentation, and a documented compliance rationale establishing that the screened entity is not a target or is subject only to unsanctioned dealing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: To inject equity or shareholder-loan capital into the Ontario corporation, route funds via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the corporation's CAD or USD account at a Schedule I Canadian bank, quoting the corporate name and Ontario incorporation number in field 59 and using the remitter's bank draft references that align with the share subscription agreement. Canada maintains no statutory 'purpose code' registry, but the receiving bank will apply a Statistics Canada ITRS transaction classification; the remitter should specify 'Direct Investment – Equity' or 'Intercompany Loan' on the wire instruction. The verification bundle must include the signed share subscription agreement, board resolution authorizing issuance, Notice of Articles or share register update, a Canadian legal opinion confirming that the injection is characterized as equity or quasi-equity for Part XIII/Part I tax purposes, and the CRS/CBCR entity classification form. For payments exceeding CAD 10,000, the bank will generate an electronic FINTRAC report; for amounts above the reporting threshold, the remitter must also provide a completed SWIFT FinRem or equivalent tax-certification form if the shareholder resides in a reportable jurisdiction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) for direct disbursement to foreign dairy suppliers and logistics providers, with the underlying commercial invoice number and commodity description in the payment narrative, and settle in USD or CAD via the Lynx/ACSS real-time systems for domestic legs or through the bank's correspondent network for cross-border legs. For principal commodity procurement, use documentary letters of credit issued by a Schedule I Canadian bank under ICC UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700/MT710), payable at sight or with deferred payment tenor, with the L/C naming the Ontario company as applicant and the foreign exporter as beneficiary; confirmations by a first-class international bank are recommended for milk-powder suppliers in jurisdictions with elevated country risk. All outbound payments must be supported by (i) the purchase contract, (ii) the pro-forma invoice, (iii) inspection certificates, (iv) CFIA export/import certifications, and (v) transport documents, and must be screened against the Canadian sanctions regime and counterparty embargo lists before transmission.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward contracts in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNY, and CAD/CHF with a Schedule I bank or an eligible credit-corporation counterparty under ISDA documentation, used to lock the CAD value of projected milk-powder export receipts and import payables for tenors up to 24 months.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) structured by a Canadian bank or its foreign affiliate, net-settled in CAD, for hedging exposure to currencies of importing jurisdictions with limited onshore convertibility (e.g., CNY if subject to settlement restrictions), provided the NDF is documented as a hedge of a genuine commercial receivable.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) exchanging fixed or floating CAD payments for USD/EUR/CHF payments, covering principal and interest cash flows on intercompany loans or on trade-finance lines, subject to an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and a collateral arrangement acceptable to the bank.

Plain-vanilla deliverable FX options (call/put structures) on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, including collars and zero-premium risk reversals, purchased for hedge-only purposes and not for speculative trading.

Exchange-traded currency futures and options on CAD and USD listed on CME Group or B3, cleared through a registered futures commission merchant and endorsed by the corporate treasury policy, primarily used for shorter-tenor tactical hedging.

Forward rate agreements (FRAs) and interest rate swaps used in conjunction with the FX hedges where the underlying trade-finance facility carries a floating-rate exposure, to neutralize the cross-currency basis risk in the overall treasury portfolio.

stage_4.stage_summary_note: Canada's open capital account and absence of FX surrender rules reduce compliance friction, while the mandatory onboarding posture for a dairy commodity trader rests on Schedule I bank account infrastructure, LC-based trade settlement, and conservative use of non-bank fintech rails, with all flows documented against FINTRAC, CFIA, and CBSA requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (ServiceOntario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the fiscal year-end of the corporation; if no fiscal year-end was established, within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing beyond 60 days triggers a CAD 50 late-filing penalty; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the Director to administratively dissolve the corporation. Directors or officers may become personally liable for continuing to transact business during default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Canada Business Corporations Act) — required if the corporation is incorporated federally and registered extra-provincially in Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director, Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or continuation; alternatively within 60 days after the annual meeting date if the Director has set a different filing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution by the Director; late returns may require a notice of non-compliance and additional revival fees before the corporation can be reinstated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Ontario Business Corporations Act and the Canada Business Corporations Act, every corporation must appoint an independent auditor at its annual meeting unless all shareholders (for a private, non-offering corporation) unanimously consent to dispense with the audit. Public or offering corporations, financial institutions, and corporations governed by specific industry statutes cannot waive the audit. There is no minimum revenue, asset, or employee threshold for private corporations; the decision to require an audit is shareholder-controlled.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises and permitted for private corporations; private corporations may elect to use Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook. Statutory financial statements must comply with the chosen framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register) recording any individual with at least 25% direct or indirect ownership, voting rights, or de jure control. Updates to the register must be made within 15 days of becoming aware of a change. Annually, management must verify the register's accuracy and, for federal corporations, confirm its existence in the annual return. The register must be kept at the registered office or another permitted location and retained for six years after the individual ceases to be significant.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)
Register of Debentures and Bondholders (if any)
Minute Book containing records of directors' and shareholders' meetings and resolutions
Register of Share Certificates issued, transferred, or cancelled
Register of Securities Ownership and Transfers (if applicable)
